title: Latency-aware shadow bridge with timed-promote oracle and automatic rollback
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a latency-aware promotion path for shadow traffic with an automated rollback oracle; configurable thresholds and timed promotes. Backwards-compatible with existing rollout policies.
description:
Motivation: We need safer, measurable promotion from shadow to canary for models that can introduce subtle latency regressions. Existing shadow->canary flows rely on correctness metrics alone and lack a structured tail-latency safety net. This PR introduces a latency-aware "timed-promote oracle" that promotes shadow workloads incrementally when latency delta and error budgets are within configured bounds, and automatically rolls back (or holds) when regressions persist for a configured window.

Summary of changes: Implement a controller and promote-oracle that 1) continuously computes per-cohort p50/p95/p99 deltas between candidate (shadow) and baseline models, 2) exposes a timed-promote state machine (observe -> prewarm -> promote -> hold), 3) wires safety checks into the rollout planner so traffic ramps only when tail-latency deltas are below thresholds, and 4) adds an automatic rollback flow that triggers if deltas exceed a threshold for N consecutive minutes. Also adds telemetry hooks, console UI flags, canary plan templates, and an e2e latency regression test harness.

What this touches (high level): controller/shadow_bridge_controller.go - main state machine and reconciliation loop; orchestrator/promote_oracle.go - decisioning logic and timed windows; telemetry/latency_enrichment.go - tagging and histograms for model_id + cohort; console/src/components/rollout/LatencyPromotePanel.tsx - UI to view latency deltas and override policies; e2e/tests/latency_pulse_test.yaml - synthetic load test to simulate tail spikes; docs/runbooks/shadow-promote-playbook.md - operational runbook and rollback playbook.

Checklist: 
- [x] Controller and oracle implementation
- [x] Unit tests for state transitions and decision boundaries
- [x] Integration test: simulated shadow->canary ramp using latency_pulse_test
- [x] Telemetry: p50/p95/p99 deltas, SLA breach counters, promote/rollback events
- [x] Console: read-only view + manual override button
- [x] Docs: runbook and API notes
- [x] Backwards compatible with existing rollout CRD

Design notes: The promote-oracle uses exponential backoff on re-promote attempts and enforces a minimum "observation window" (configurable, default 5m) before any promote. Decision thresholds are split across two dimensions: delta latency (absolute ms) and relative tail amplification (percentage). The oracle also consults per-customer SLO tags so tenants with stricter latency SLOs can opt for stricter thresholds. Rollback action is idempotent and records a snapshot to the rollback journal to allow replay.

Operational expectations: When enabled, this flow will introduce additional telemetry (a few new histograms and counters). There is a small CPU cost in the controller to compute deltas across cohorts (~5-15ms per reconciliation, measured on dev cluster). Default behavior is opt-in per rollout; no rollout will change behavior unless a rollout config references the new "latency_promote" strategy.

Testing summary: Unit test coverage added for promote_oracle state machine (85% on new files). Integration e2e test simulates a model with a slow tail; the test verifies that the oracle prevents promotion when p99 delta > 25ms and that it rolls back if the regression persists for the configured 10m hold window. CI initially had a flaky e2e timing test (latency_pulse_test) which was fixed by increasing the synthetic pulse duration; the pipeline was re-run and passed.

Backward compatibility and migration: The rollout CRD adds an optional "latency_promote" section. Existing rollouts remain unchanged. Admins can enable at rollout creation time or via the console. If a rollout references the new field but the controller version is old, the rollout will be rejected with a clear validation error (docs contain migration steps).

Security and privacy: No model data or PII is changed or exported. Telemetry uses model_id hashes and tenant IDs consistent with existing telemetry policies.

References: Linear ENG-4021 (latency-aware promotions), ENG-4087 (promote oracle design), internal doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4021/latency-promote-oracle, runbook: docs/runbooks/shadow-promote-playbook.md

Merge plan: Squash merge. Rollout controller feature gated behind feature flag "latency_promote_v1". After merge: monitor rollout-promote-events and p99_delta metrics on staging for 48h, then flip console opt-in toggles for selected tenants.

If something goes wrong: runbook includes immediate rollback command and a snapshot restore path that can be executed via the CLI (scripts/rollback_snapshot.sh).

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Please clarify how cohort sizing affects delta computation; are we normalizing for tiny cohorts? (requested change)
Maya Chen: Answered - we apply a minimum-sample floor and fallback to bootstrapped estimates for cohorts < 200 requests; added tests to cover both paths.
Priya Nair: Can we avoid excessive histogram cardinality when tagging by model+cohort? Concern about metrics cardinality on large tenants. (requested change)
Maya Chen: Addressed - switched to aggregated model hash + coarse cohort bucket tags for telemetry, updated latency_enrichment.go, and added a note in the runbook about metric retention.
Ethan Brooks: lgtm after CI fixes. Also suggested an additional e2e to exercise a slow transient (optional).
